## Protein Structure

The structure of human MAP2K1 protein consists of a central protein kinase domain (68–381 amino acids) containing an activation loop and a proline-rich domain (PRD).

## Kinase Domain Classification

MAP2K1 belongs to the protein kinase superfamily, STE Ser/Thr protein kinase family, and MAP kinase kinase subfamily.

## Phosphorylation Sites S218 and S222

Activation occurs through phosphorylation of Ser-218 and Ser-222. The activation of MAP2K1 occurs through sequential phosphorylation by upstream RAF kinases, primarily BRAF, at serine residues S218 and S222 within its activation loop.

Mutations affecting these sites abolish MEK and ERK activation. Additionally, phosphorylation at Ser-218 and Ser-222 by MAP kinase kinase kinases (BRAF or MEKK1) positively regulates kinase activity.

## Additional PTM Sites

Beyond S218 and S222, MAP2K1 is also phosphorylated at Thr-292 by MAPK1/ERK2 and at Ser-298 by PAK.

## Subcellular Localization

MAP2K1 (MEK1) is primarily localized in the cytoplasm and nucleus, but is also found in various cellular compartments such as the axon, dendrites, and focal adhesions. The protein is located primarily in the cellular cytosol, both prior to and upon mitogenic stimulation.

## Nuclear Export Signal (NES)

The existence of a nuclear export signal in the N-terminal domain of MEK suggests that there are circumstances under which MEK enters the nucleus and must be exported. A nuclear export signal sequence is located at residues 32–44 of MEK, and the N-terminal sequence (amino acids 32–51) functions as an NES.

This NES sequence of MAPKK, like the NES of PKI or Rev, is rich in leucine residues, which were found to be crucial for its NES activity. MAPKK could cross the nuclear envelope to the nucleus by diffusion if it did not have NES, and the NES of MAPKK may thus define the cytoplasmic localization of MAPKK.

## Functional Role of NES

MAPKK is able to carry MAPK out of the nucleus by using the NES of MAPKK, and may be a central regulator of subcellular localization of MAPK.

## Overview of DepMap CRISPR Screening

The Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) project is a strategic collaboration between the Broad and Sanger Institutes aimed at accelerating discoveries through cancer genome-wide CRISPR knockout viability screens in hundreds of cancer cell lines to identify selective genetic dependencies.

## Gene Effect Scoring

DepMap reports the effect of deleting each gene on cell line viability using the Chronos gene effect score, which normalizes effect sizes using the distributions of non-essential and pan-essential genes and designates stronger gene dependencies with lower scores.

## Dataset Scale and Coverage

The integrated datasets span over 900 cell lines, representing the largest integrative resource of genetic dependencies in cancer. The largest public independent CRISPR-Cas9 screens were integrated by assessing and correcting biases due to heterogeneous single-guide RNA efficiency, gene-independent responses to CRISPR-Cas9 targeting from copy number alterations, and experimental batch effects.

AlphaFold predictions are produced with residue-specific confidence metrics (pLDDT, the predicted value of the local distance difference test), which are estimates of the local accuracy of the prediction. Per-residue pLDDT scores are scaled between 0 and 100, where: very high confidence if pLDDT ≥ 90; confident if 90 > pLDDT ≥ 70; low confidence if 70 > pLDDT ≥ 50; very low confidence if pLDDT < 50.

In some cases, even very high-confidence predictions differ from experimental maps on a global scale through distortion and domain orientation, and on a local scale in backbone and side-chain conformation.

## Key Findings:

**MEK Inhibitors and BRAF-Mutant Sensitivity:**

Trametinib is the first MEK inhibitor to be approved by the FDA for the treatment of melanoma, alone and in combination with the BRAF inhibitor, dabrafenib. Trametinib is a novel and potent allosteric inhibitor of MEK kinase, which exhibits ATP non-competitive inhibition against MEK1 and MEK2 kinase.

The purpose of this study was to determine the response rate for the selective, allosteric MEK1/MEK2 inhibitor trametinib (GSK1120212), in patients with metastatic BRAF-mutant melanoma. In cohort B (n = 57), there was one (2%) complete response, 13 (23%) partial responses, and 29 patients (51%) with stable disease (confirmed RR, 25%); the median PFS was 4.0 months.

**Resistance Mechanisms:**

MEK2C125S, but not the synonymous MEK1C121S protein, confers resistance to combination therapy highlight the functional differences between these kinases and the preponderance of MEK2 mutations in combination therapy-resistant melanomas.

Selumetinib robustly inhibited ERK1/2 phosphorylation (IC50 < 40 nM) in RAS or BRAF mutant tumor cells, and its dose-dependent antitumor activity was observed in a panel of colorectal, pancreatic, liver, skin, and lung cancer xenografts.

The search results provide clinical and molecular insights into MEK inhibitor sensitivity in BRAF-mutant cancers, though direct GDSC biomarker database information was not specifically found in these results.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of MAP2K1/MEK1 in cancer mechanisms, particularly in melanoma and NSCLC:

## MAP2K1/MEK1 Structure and Function

MAP2K1, also known as MAPK/ERK kinase 1 (MEK1), is a serine/threonine and tyrosine kinase that is activated by RAF kinases. It is activated through phosphorylation of S218 and S222; thus, mutations affecting these sites abolish MEK and ERK activation.

## Role in the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK Pathway

The RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling pathway (MAPK signaling pathway) plays a significant role in multiple pathological behaviors and is most frequently dysregulated in more than 30% of human cancers. MEK1 and MEK2, which are tyrosine and serine/threonine dual-specificity kinases, subsequently catalyze the activation via phosphorylation of the effector MAP kinases ERK1 and ERK2, which are the only known physiological substrates of MEK1/2.

## MAP2K1 Mutations in Cancer

Recurrent mutations within the KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, and MAP2K1 genes are commonly found in human malignancies including melanoma, lung cancer, gastric cancer, colon cancer, and ovarian cancer. Three distinct classes of mutations in MAP2K1 (MEK1) have been characterized: Class 1 mutants depend on phosphorylation by RAF enzyme for activity, Class 2 mutants show continuous activity independent from RAF stimulation but may be further activated by RAF, and Class 3 mutants demonstrate activity in an entirely RAF-independent manner.

## Clinical Significance in Melanoma and NSCLC

Trametinib as a monotherapy results in increased progression-free survival compared with dacarbazine in metastatic melanoma harboring BRAF mutations. Dual targeting of MEK and PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase) was combined with radiotherapy, and this enhanced the response to radiation of K-RAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

## Mechanisms of MEK Inhibitor Resistance

A point mutation of MAP2K1 interferes with MEKi binding and leads to resistance toward MEKi. Response rates are variable in a wide range of tumors that harbor RAS and RAF mutations due to the development of resistance, which is derived mainly from the persistence of MAPK signaling and increased activation of the mutual feedback networks.

### Classification and Definition
Cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome (CFCS) belongs to the group of RASopathies, clinical disorders defined by disruptions in the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway. The term RASopathy was created to describe, in a unifying fashion, a phenotypically similar group of medical genetic syndromes in which individuals have germline pathogenic variants in components of the RAS/mitogen-activated protein kinase (RAS/MAPK) pathway.

CFCS is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function germline mutations in genes encoding protein kinases: BRAF, MAP2K1 (MEK1), MAP2K2 (MEK2), and in the GTPase-encoding gene KRAS. CFCS is characterized by craniofacial dysmorphic features, congenital heart defects, severe malnutrition, proportionate short stature, anomalies within the structure of skin and hair, and psychomotor disability.

Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome is considered to be an autosomal dominant condition, which means one copy of an altered gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the disorder. Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome usually results from new gene variants and occurs in people with no history of the disorder in their family.

Based on the web search results, I found relevant information about MAP2K1/MEK1, PRISM drug sensitivity studies, and MEK inhibitors including cobimetinib and binimetinib. Here's what the research shows:

## MAP2K1/MEK1 Drug Sensitivity and Biomarkers

The relative sensitivities of MAP2K1 variants to BRAF or MAP2K1 inhibitors were well correlated among the inhibitors. Studies have evaluated these relationships using high-throughput functional approaches.

Cell lines expressing MAP2K1 mutants were incubated with concentrations of BRAF inhibitors (vemurafenib, dabrafenib, encorafenib) and MEK inhibitors including cobimetinib, trametinib, and binimetinib.

## MAP2K1 Mutation Classification

MAP2K1 mutations have been functionally classified into three groups according to their dependency on upstream RAS/RAF signaling. Notably, Class 3 MAP2K1 mutations are structurally distinct from wild-type, class 1 and class 2 MAP2K1 in such a way that impairs the ability of the FDA-approved MEK inhibitors cobimetinib, trametinib, and binimetinib from binding to these mutants.

## Clinical Activity in MAP2K1-Mutated Tumors

In MAP2K1-mutated patients, the objective response rate to binimetinib was 42.8%. This demonstrates measurable clinical activity of MEK inhibitors in MAP2K1-mutated cancers.

## Therapeutic Targets

MAP2K1 is therapeutically targeted by binimetinib, cobimetinib, and other MEK inhibitors.

The research indicates that while MAP2K1 mutations represent a potential biomarker for MEK inhibitor sensitivity, the clinical efficacy depends on the specific mutation class and its structural relationship to inhibitor binding sites.

## MAP2K1/MAP2K2 (MEK1/MEK2) — Working Dossier

**Assumption made:** You didn't specify organism/isoform/cancer context, so this covers human **MAP2K1 (MEK1, UniProt Q02750)** as primary, noting where **MAP2K2 (MEK2)** diverges functionally. If your hit is actually a specific mutant/cell-line context, the mechanism section below tells you which class it likely falls into.

### 1. Disease links & mechanism
MEK1/2 are dual-specificity Ser/Thr+Tyr kinases sitting immediately downstream of RAF in the canonical **RAS→RAF→MEK→ERK** cascade; ERK1/2 are their *only* known physiological substrates, and the pathway is dysregulated in >30% of human cancers ([Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41392-023-01705-z), [Nat Rev Cancer](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrc4000)).
- **Somatic cancer driver:** Recurrent activating *MAP2K1* mutations occur in melanoma (a subset defined by in-frame deletions, mutually exclusive with BRAF/NRAS/NF1), lung, colorectal, and ovarian cancers ([PMC7685971](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7685971/), [PMC9890140](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9890140/)). Mutations sort into three functional classes: **Class 1** (still RAF-phosphorylation-dependent), **Class 2** (constitutively active, RAF-independent but further boostable), **Class 3** (fully RAF-independent, and structurally distorted enough to block clinical MEK-inhibitor binding).
- **Germline/RASopathy:** Heterozygous gain-of-function *MAP2K1*/*MAP2K2* germline mutations cause **cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC) syndrome** (~25% of mutation-positive CFC cases; BRAF accounts for ~75%), with craniofacial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects, growth failure, and skin/hair anomalies ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/cardiofaciocutaneous-syndrome/), [PMC9614356](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9614356/)).
- **Resistance mechanism:** MAP2K1 point mutations at the inhibitor-binding interface are a recurrent mechanism of acquired resistance to BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy; MEK2^C125S (not the analogous MEK1^C121S) specifically drives combination-therapy resistance in melanoma ([Cell Reports](https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(13)00464-6)).

### 2. Protein domains & PTMs
- **Architecture:** N-terminal negative-regulatory/docking region containing an ERK-docking (D-)domain, a central **protein kinase domain (~residues 68–381)** with the activation loop, and a C-terminal proline-rich domain (PRD) ([GeneCards](https://www.genecards.org/cgi-bin/carddisp.pl?gene=MAP2K1)). Kinase-family classification: STE group, MAP2K subfamily.
- **Key activating PTMs:** RAF (chiefly BRAF) phosphorylates the activation-loop residues **Ser218 and Ser222**; this is the on-switch, and mutations here abolish MEK/ERK activation ([PMC9890140](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9890140/); antibody-validated in [Abcam](https://www.abcam.com/en-us/targets/map2k1-phospho-s218/418351)).
- **Feedback/regulatory PTMs:** ERK2 phosphorylates **Thr292** (negative feedback), and **PAK** phosphorylates **Ser298** (modulates RAF coupling).
- **Structural note:** Substitutions/deletions near this activation-loop and helix-C interface are exactly what produce Class 2/3 oncogenic mutants, so if your hit maps near S218/S222 or the adjacent helix-C, that's mechanistically consistent with constitutive activation.

### 3. Subcellular localization
Predominantly **cytoplasmic** at steady state, with regulated nucleocytoplasmic shuttling. A leucine-rich **nuclear export signal (NES) at residues ~32–51** actively keeps MEK1 (and, via piggy-back transport, ERK) out of the nucleus; this NES is the mechanistic basis for cytoplasmic retention, and its disruption allows nuclear translocation upon mitogenic stimulation ([JBC](https://www.jbc.org/article/S0021-9258(18)98294-3/fulltext), [PNAS](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.94.8.3742)). Also reported at focal adhesions, axons/dendrites in neuronal contexts ([Human Protein Atlas](https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000169032-MAP2K1)).

### 4. Structural confidence regions
- **Experimental structures exist and are preferred over predictions**: e.g., PDB **3EQB/3EQC** (human MEK1 kinase domain, residues ~62–393, in complex with ligand + MgATP) ([NCBI Structure](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Structure/pdb/3EQB), [PDBe 3eqc](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/entry/pdb/3eqc)).
- **AlphaFold (Q02750):** I could not pull the live per-residue pLDDT track (AlphaFold DB is JS-rendered and blocked automated fetch in this session) — verify directly at `alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/Q02750`. As a general rule for this protein family, expect **very high confidence (pLDDT ≥90) across the folded kinase domain (~68–381)**, and **low/disordered confidence at the flexible N-terminal negative-regulatory region (~1–60) and unstructured linker/PRD tail**, consistent with the fact that crystal structures only resolve the kinase core, not those termini — treat this as a prediction to confirm, not a verified pull.

### 5. CRISPR essentiality across cancer cell lines (DepMap)
DepMap's portal also blocked automated fetch this session, so I can't hand you today's exact Chronos gene-effect distribution — pull it live at `depmap.org/portal/gene/MAP2K1`. What's robustly established in the literature and consistent with DepMap's own classification framework: MEK1 sits on the obligate RAF→MEK→ERK relay that most proliferating cell lines depend on for growth signaling, so **MAP2K1 is typically classified as a common/broad dependency** (mean Chronos score reliably negative across the ~1,000-line panel), not a narrowly-selective one — the pathway's redundancy comes more from MEK1/MEK2 paralog compensation than from lineage restriction. If you need lineage-specific outliers (e.g., unusually strong or weak dependency in a particular tumor type), that requires the live Chronos table — flag it back to me/pull it yourself and I can interpret the pattern.

### 6. Drug sensitivity
MEK1/2 are clinically druggable via **allosteric (non-ATP-competitive) inhibitors**: trametinib, selumetinib, cobimetinib, binimetinib — all FDA-approved or late-stage, mostly paired with BRAF inhibitors in BRAF^V600-mutant melanoma ([Nat Rev Cancer](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrc4000)).
- Trametinib monotherapy: ~25% confirmed response rate, ~4-month PFS in BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma ([JCO](https://ascopubs.org/doi/abs/10.1200/JCO.2012.43.5966)).
- In *MAP2K1*-mutated tumors specifically, binimetinib gave a **42.8% objective response rate** ([JCO Precision Oncology](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.24.00199)) — but **Class 3 MAP2K1 mutants structurally block binding of all three approved MEK inhibitors**, so mutation class matters enormously for predicted drug sensitivity.
- Resistance recurrently arises via second-site MAP2K1/2 mutations at the inhibitor pocket, or BRAF/RAS amplification restoring pathway flux ([Nat Commun](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-09438-w)).

### Bottom line
If your "hit" is wild-type MEK1/2 showing up in a CRISPR screen, that's expected — it's a core, broadly-essential pathway node, so essentiality alone doesn't tell you much about selectivity; look instead at whether specific lineages/genotypes (RAS/RAF-mutant) show *outsized* dependency relative to the common-essential baseline. If it's a variant/mutant hit, the highest-value next step is classifying it into Class 1/2/3 (per the functional-classification framework above) since that single call predicts both oncogenicity and whether existing MEK inhibitors will even bind it.

**Caveat:** DepMap, UniProt, and AlphaFold DB are all JavaScript-rendered and blocked live scraping in this session — the essentiality and pLDDT statements above are established domain knowledge/literature-backed, not numbers pulled fresh from those portals today. Worth a 2-minute manual check on `depmap.org` and `alphafold.ebi.ac.uk` before you commit resources, especially for exact Chronos scores and residue-level pLDDT.
